body:
maya: Quick sync 1: proposing a slim onboarding strip pinned below the top nav for first-run users. Contains 4 micro-steps: Connect, Sample app, Run demo, Tour. Persistent but closable. Opinions?
sam: Nice anchor. Concern: the strip is cramped on tablet. Can we collapse to icons + short labels at narrow widths?
olivia: Collapse sounds good. Must ensure each collapsed item still has accessible name + tooltip. Keyboard + screenreader flows are critical.
kai: Dismissal rules: don't hide forever on accidental close. Maybe respect a dismiss TTL (7 days) and a harder opt-out after explicit "Don't show again". No telemetry unless user opts in.
maya: Agreed on TTL. UX decision point: explicit 'Don't show again' vs just a close that toggles TTL. Which is less disruptive?
nora: From onboarding metrics I prefer explicit opt-out. Close should be reversible via Help menu. Also add a subtle progress indicator so users know they've completed X/4 steps.
sam: Microcopy ideas: A) "Start your first project" B) "Complete setup (4 quick steps)" C) "Ready in minutes: connect & try" — which feels best?
olivia: 'Start your first project' wins for friendliness. 'Complete' feels heavy. Also avoid numbers in the strip copy; show count visually instead.
ux-bot: Experiment scheduled: onboard_strip_copy_v1 vs onboard_strip_copy_v2. Events: onboard_strip_impression, onboard_strip_cta_click, onboard_strip_dismiss. Funnels: onboard_start -> sample_run -> demo_complete.
maya: Accessibility checklist: focusable elements (Tab), visible focus ring, aria-label on each pill, aria-live region for progress updates, color + icon state, and ensure contrast >= 4.5 for body text.
sa m: tiny nit: ensure dismiss button has aria-label="Close onboarding strip" and not just "Close" so screenreader context is clear. Also use separate focusable control for the explicit opt-out.
kai: Mobile: tap-to-expand each step into a small sheet with a CTA and a small explanation. Ensure tap targets >=44px and allow swipe-down to close.
maya: I'll update Figma with collapsed state, expanded sheet flow, and the 7-day TTL vs permanent opt-out toggles. Posting frames in #design by EOD. Thanks all! :sparkles:
